meta.title: Monthly active users across available months
meta.question: How did monthly active users change across the available months?
meta.author: Codex

items: Checks refer to numbered evidence JSONL files in the run folder.
MAU counts distinct identified people, not sessions; unidentified sessions are shown separately.
MAU
Distinct resolved users with a session active during a complete UTC calendar month.
Unidentified sessions
Sessions that cannot be attributed under the approved identity rule; excluded from MAU.

blocks.text: Monthly active users rose in every available month, from 7,937 in April to 11,447 in September 2026: an increase of 3,510 users (44.2%). Growth slowed to 1.6% in July before accelerating in August. (Check 4)

blocks.title: Interpretation
blocks.text: These figures describe the trend, not its causes. Unidentified sessions are excluded and do not translate directly into a number of missing people.

items: Period: six complete UTC calendar months, April through September 2026; coverage ends 2026-10-01 00:00 UTC, exclusive.
Definition: approved mau v1.1; a user is active if a resolved session overlaps the month, including browsing-only activity.
Build: 3a0dbed21d2f45958aefa2887a0cadd8, succeeded 2026-11-09 11:16:56 UTC. Checks 1–4.
Selected Gold monthly KPI because its grain, UTC coverage and MAU definition match the question.
Checked build reconciliation and independently recounted monthly distinct users from Silver; all six values match. (Checks 2, 4, 6)
Checked session identity, duplicates and spans in Silver. (Check 5)
Month-on-month changes: May +1,197 (15.1%); June +842 (9.2%); July +162 (1.6%); August +733 (7.2%); September +576 (5.3%).
MAU is non-additive: do not sum monthly counts to obtain unique users across the period.
Unidentified sessions range from 2,286 to 3,703 per month and are excluded from MAU; their number of distinct people and effect on the trend are unknown. (Check 4)

Session-start check found no duplicate IDs, invalid spans or identity-link mismatches. One session spanning August and September explains why September has 3,702 unresolved sessions started in September but 3,703 touching September. (Checks 4–5)

The build records successful source-to-Gold MAU reconciliation and mau v1.1. Its registry file SHA-256 differs from the current registry file, so exact registry-file equivalence is unverified despite the matching version label. The builder hash matches the current builder. (Check 2)
The dataset is synthetic; its activity coverage is declared complete for the fixture, not evidence of real-world completeness.
The trend alone does not establish why MAU changed. No causal hypotheses were tested for this descriptive question.
If an explanation is needed, investigate acquisition and retention using the approved growth-accounting definition and check whether excluded unidentified traffic changes interpretation.
